correctness.rationale: Directly computed the double ideal quotient I^v=S-(S-I). For I != S, S-I comprises conductor tail >=2m and those m+i in [m,2m-r-1] not struck by windows E_x=[L-x,L+r-1-x] intersect [0,L-1] from lower added x; I^v contains all terminal gaps and precisely lower x whose entire E_x is already covered. The monotone fixed points are unions Z of the length-r truncated windows, with I_Z=S union upper terminal gap block union {x:E_x subset Z}; each nonempty window ensures injectivity. Such unions are exactly words without short strictly internal one-runs; endpoints may be shorter. Decomposing one-runs and nonempty zero-runs yields the rational generating function. D_r(z)=(1-z)^2-z^(r+1) has one dominant simple positive zero rho_r, giving coefficient asymptotic rho_r^-L/[(1-rho_r)(2(1-rho_r)+(r+1)rho_r^r)]. Roots increase strictly to 1 in r; for r=3 the root is the reciprocal golden ratio. Independently enumerated all normalized gap subsets and computed the defining double quotients for twelve (m,r) instances r=3,4,5 and L=1..4; their exact sets match the word construction. SymPy coefficients at L=1..9 match 2,4,7,11,17,27,44,72,117. The infinite assertion follows from the window algebra and singularity argument, not enumeration.

value.rationale: Determines the complete translation-class spectrum and inclusion order of divisorial ideals in a natural two-parameter terminal-gap semigroup family, with a regular-language bijection, rational series and an r-dependent exact exponential growth law. An arbitrary small finite case would be insufficient, but the all-r classification and growth are substantive invariants motivated by current reflexive-ideal theory.

final_claim: For m>=r+1 and r>=3, normalized reflexive relative ideals of S={0} union [m,2m-r-1] union [2m,infinity) are S and the I_Z indexed by length-(m-r) binary words with every interior one-run of length >=r. Their count is 1+a_r(m-r) with generating series 1/(1-z)+z/[(1-z)((1-z)^2-z^(r+1))], and fixed-r growth rate rho_r^-1 where (1-rho_r)^2=rho_r^(r+1).
limitations: Only one terminal consecutive gap block, r>=3 and m>=r+1; excludes r=2 already treated and all nonterminal separated patterns; fixed-r asymptotic not uniform as r grows. General ideal decomposition in the prior source is acknowledged.
